c.tagline: Germany's harbor city of red brick, canals, and Reeperbahn nights.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are metered and regulated; hail one at ranks, on the street, or via the Free Now app. A ride across the centre runs roughly 10-15 EUR.

emergency.note: 112 reaches ambulance and fire across the EU; 110 is the direct police line. Both are free from any phone.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: St. Pauli/Reeperbahn nightlife — watch for scams, pickpockets and aggressive touts

hood_desc: Hamburg's walkable core around the Rathaus, Jungfernstieg and the Binnenalster lake, blending the historic Altstadt with the shopping and business streets of Neustadt; best for first-timers who want everything within reach.

The city's raucous nightlife district built around the Reeperbahn, Europe's longest strip of bars, clubs and live-music venues, plus the Sunday fish market; suits travelers who want to go out late and stay in the thick of it.
A trendy, left-leaning quarter of street art, indie boutiques, cafes and buzzing bars just north of Altona; a former counterculture stronghold that draws a younger, alternative crowd.
Hamburg's sleek modern waterfront district on former docklands beside the Speicherstadt warehouses, anchored by the Elbphilharmonie concert hall, with design hotels, promenades and quiet river views.
A formerly independent town turned laid-back local district west of the centre, full of shops, restaurants, the Altona fish market and Elbe-side parks; a relaxed base for seeing everyday Hamburg.

water.note: Tap water is safe and of high quality.

transit.hours: U-Bahn and S-Bahn run roughly 4:30am-1am on weekdays and all night on Friday and Saturday nights; night buses cover the gaps midweek.
transit.pay: There are no tap-in gates: buy tickets in the hvv app or from station machines (cards accepted) and have them ready before boarding. A Hamburg AB single costs about 4.10 EUR (~US$4.50) and a day ticket about 8.20 EUR; one ticket covers U-Bahn, S-Bahn, buses and the public harbour ferries. App tickets usually get a ~7% discount, and the Deutschland-Ticket (63 EUR/month) covers local transit nationwide.

transit.m: S-Bahn S1 to Jungfernstieg city centre (30 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up the bill or leaving 5-10% for good service is customary. Tell the server the total you want to pay as you hand over the money.

landmarks: Elbphilharmonie
A dazzling glass concert hall rising like a crystalline wave atop a brick warehouse on the Elbe, now the defining silhouette of modern Hamburg.
Hamburg Rathaus
A lavishly ornamented neo-Renaissance city hall with 647 rooms, standing grandly over its own market square in the heart of the city.
Speicherstadt
The world's largest historic warehouse district, a UNESCO-listed maze of red-brick facades, canals, and iron bridges especially magical when lit at night.
St. Michaelis Church (Der Michel)
Hamburg's iconic baroque church tower, whose observation deck delivers the city's best rooftop-and-harbor panorama.
Landungsbrücken
Hamburg's grand floating harbor piers, alive with ferries, ships, and views across the busy port that built the city's fortune.
Miniatur Wunderland
The world's largest model railway, a jaw-dropping miniature universe of tiny cities, airports, and landscapes hidden inside a Speicherstadt warehouse.
Binnenalster & Alster Lakes
A shimmering inner-city lake ringed by grand facades and sailboats, perfect for a scenic stroll or classic postcard shot of Hamburg's skyline.
Reeperbahn
Europe's most famous nightlife strip in St. Pauli, a neon-lit stretch of clubs, theaters, and bars synonymous with Hamburg after dark.
HafenCity
Europe's largest inner-city redevelopment, a striking waterfront district of contemporary architecture built out into the harbor around the Elbphilharmonie.
Hamburg Cruise Terminal & Port
One of Europe's biggest and busiest seaports, where container giants, historic sailing ships, and harbor cranes create a dramatic industrial skyline.

train.note: Nearly all long-distance trains call at Hamburg Hauptbahnhof, and many also stop at Dammtor and Hamburg-Altona - Altona is the terminus for several ICE runs and for the Zurich Nightjet, so check which station your ticket names. Since December 2019 Copenhagen trains no longer use the Puttgarden-Rodby train ferry; they take the long way round through Flensburg, Kolding and Odense over the Great Belt link, about 4h45, and from 2026 mostly use DSB Talgo EuroCity Express sets. Snalltaget also runs a seasonal daytime service through to Copenhagen, Malmo and Stockholm. Berlin is under 2h and Munich around 6h.

bus.note: International coaches use the ZOB Hamburg on Adenauerallee, immediately east of the Hauptbahnhof and linked to it by a short covered walk. It is a proper staffed terminal with a ticket office, lockers and a heated waiting hall, although booking online is still cheaper. Copenhagen takes roughly 5-6 hours including the Danish border, Berlin about 3h30 and Amsterdam around 6h30; Schengen means no routine passport control, but carry ID.

intl.to: Helgoland (Germany) - Halunder Jet catamaran from the Landungsbrucken St. Pauli

ferry.note: Hamburg is Germany's largest port but no longer has a scheduled international car ferry - the old North Sea services to England ended years ago, so for Britain, Scandinavia or the Baltic you travel on to Lubeck-Travemunde (about 1h by train), Kiel or Rostock, or to the Dutch ports. What Hamburg does have is the seasonal Halunder Jet catamaran out to the island of Helgoland, running roughly from spring to autumn from the Landungsbrucken St. Pauli and taking most of a day there and back. HADAG harbour ferries are part of the hvv public transport network and are the cheapest harbour cruise in the city - line 62 to Finkenwerder is the classic. Cruise ships use separate terminals at Steinwerder, Altona and HafenCity.

half.name: Lübeck

half.name: Lüneburg
half.blurb: Medieval salt-trading town with a tilted town hall and gabled brick merchant houses.

half.name: Bremen
half.blurb: Hanseatic city with the Bremen Town Musicians statue, a UNESCO market square, and the Böttcherstraße art district.

full.name: Sylt
full.blurb: North Sea island of dunes and thatched-roof villages, reached by train across a causeway through the Wadden Sea.
